segments: Chronography of Barhebraeus.
Those inside also dug and came out against those outside,
and killed those whom they found inside the trench,
and they returned and built a wall opposite the trench.
Those outside, however, dug beneath two {OCR?} other towers.
And when the bastions were close to falling,
Zangi the Atabeg sent word to the Edessenes and said:
"Take two men from us to yourselves,
and send two men to see the bastions that are close to falling, and surrender the city before you are taken by the sword and perish."
Papa (Papias), however, the head of the Franks in Edessa,
because he relied on Joscelin and on the king of Jerusalem to come to their aid,
would not be persuaded,
nor did he heed, but mocked Zangi.
Then those outside cast fire onto the timbers that were propping up the bastions,
and they fell.
And when the Turks began to enter through the breach,
the people of the city from within, along with Papias and the bishops, stood at the breach,
and they held back the Turks from entering.
And the breach was filled with heaps of the slain, both from those inside and from those outside.
And when all the people had gathered at the breach,
the Turks saw that the wall was emptied of defenders,
and they set up ladders and went up.
And when those inside saw that the Turks had gained control of the wall,
their hands grew slack,
and they began to flee to the citadel of the city.
And from then on,

what mouth is not stopped from recounting! Or what finger does not tremble to write of the disaster that occurred at the time of the third hour on Saturday, the third of the Latter Kanun, when the Turks entered with their swords drawn, drinking the blood of old men and children,
of men and women,
of priests and deacons,
of solitary monks,
of virgin nuns,
of suckling babes,
of bridegrooms and brides.
Oh, what a bitter tale! The city of Abgar, the friend of Christ, was trampled underfoot because of our iniquity! Woe for the distress!
Children disowned parents,
and parents [disowned] children; a mother forgot compassion for her offspring! And everyone ran to the top of the mountain.
And the aged priests, who were carrying the reliquaries of the martyrs, when they saw the wrath,
that which the prophet said:
"I will bear the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned"—
(Micah 7:9)—
therefore they did not flee,
nor did they cease from prayer,
until they were silenced
